title: The Cost of Priority
briefing: The priority freight corridor chosen earlier has kept lifeline deliveries moving, but ordinary traders now face missed contracts and mounting fees.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Opening general traffic at peak hours would delay filter deliveries needed to keep water plants operating.
private_intelligence.community: Small traders want a published exit condition; repeated emergency extensions are being read as a permanent two-tier system.
private_intelligence.economy: Freight firms will waive late fees if the city guarantees future slots, transferring present debt into tomorrow's capacity.
private_intelligence.safety: Food and medicine inventories are recovering unevenly, so a single end date may restore traffic before some lifelines are secure.

choices.title: Publish Staged Reopening
choices.description: Reopen audited off-peak slots and fund limited debt mediation.
choices.consequence: A visible path back to trade rebuilds confidence, while reduced corridor efficiency and mediation consume resources.

choices.title: Guarantee Future Freight Slots
choices.description: Offer fee waivers backed by reserved future capacity.
choices.consequence: Immediate cash pressure eases and trade resumes, but the promised slots constrain repairs and create later safety bottlenecks.

choices.title: Extend Lifeline Priority
choices.description: Maintain the corridor until all critical inventories meet the target.
choices.consequence: Lifeline stores stabilize, but extended exclusions deepen trader losses and distrust of emergency authority.
